findings.name: Disabled Veterans School Tax Credit
findings.description: Delaware provides a tax credit against 100% of non-vocational school district property tax on a primary residence for veterans who receive 100% disability compensation from the VA based on service-connected, permanent and total disability (including individual unemployability) or a 100% VA disability rating, and who have held legal domicile in Delaware for the past 3 years. Enacted via House Bill 214 (with House Amendment 1), signed August 10, 2021. Applications for the upcoming tax year are due April 30. A separate county-level exemption (available in New Castle, Kent, and Sussex counties) fully exempts county property taxes and local school taxes for a disabled veteran with a 100% VA-rated service-connected permanent and total disability, or who receives 100% disability compensation due to individual unemployability. Recipients may not claim both this credit and the Senior School Property Tax Credit; property tax bills must be paid in full by year-end to remain eligible in subsequent years.
findings.value: Credit against 100% of non-vocational school district property tax on primary residence; separate county-level full exemption of county + local school property tax available in New Castle, Kent, and Sussex counties
otherReqs: Must have held legal domicile in Delaware for the past 3 years
Applies only to primary residence
Applications due April 30 for the upcoming tax year
Cannot be combined with the Senior School Property Tax Credit
Property tax bills must be paid in full by year-end to remain eligible in subsequent years
documentation: Valid driver's license or state ID
findings.legalCitation: Delaware House Bill 214 (House Amendment 1), signed August 10, 2021
findings.sourceExcerpt: Qualified persons must receive 100% disability compensation from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (USDVA) based on service-connected, permanent and total disability based on individual unemployability or a 100% disability rating, and have held legal domicile in Delaware for the past 3 years. The credit applies to 100% of non-vocational school district property tax and may only be used against property taxes assessed on a primary residence. Applications for the upcoming tax year are due April 30th.

findings.name: Disabled American Veterans (DAV) License Plate
findings.description: Delaware issues a Disabled American Veterans (DAV) license plate, with a DAV/Special Parking variant available for veterans who also need disabled-parking designation. Veterans must provide official VA documentation of a service-connected disability received during a time of war or conflict. Applications are submitted via the DMV's DAV plate application forms (standard or Special Parking version).
findings.value: Specialty DAV license plate; DAV/Special Parking variant available
otherReqs: Service-connected disability (as determined by the VA) received during a time of war or conflict
Official VA documentation required with application
documentation: Official VA documentation of service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans must have a service-connected disability (as determined by the VA) they received during a time of war or conflict. Applicants will be required to provide official documentation from the VA that they have a service-connected disability. Two plate variants are available: Disabled American Veterans (standard) and DAV / Special Parking.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting, Fishing & Trapping License Exemption
findings.description: Delaware residents (and non-residents) who are veterans with a VA-rated service-connected disability of 60% or greater are eligible for a complete, lifetime exemption from hunting, fishing, and trapping license fees, administered by the Division of Fish and Wildlife. Applicants complete the Veterans with Disabilities Exempt Application and submit it to the Division; processing takes up to 4 weeks. Military patients hospitalized in military facilities may also qualify with written certification from their commanding officer documenting disability status and station location.
findings.value: Complete lifetime exemption from hunting, fishing, and trapping license fees
otherReqs: VA-rated service-connected disability of 60% or greater
Complete the Veterans with Disabilities Exempt Application
Applies to residents and non-residents meeting the disability threshold
Processing takes up to 4 weeks
findings.agency: Delaware Division of Fish and Wildlife (DNREC)
documentation: VA documentation of 60%+ service-connected disability rating
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans must have at least a 60% service-connected disability rating to qualify for this exemption. The exemption covers hunting, fishing, and trapping licenses. Applicants must complete the Veterans with Disabilities Exempt Application form and submit it directly to the Division of Fish and Wildlife. The agency requests allowing up to 4 weeks for processing.

findings.name: State Merit Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: Delaware adds preference points to the total ranking score of veterans applying for original entrance to State Merit employment: 10 points for disabled veterans and 5 points for other eligible veterans who served on active duty and were honorably discharged or discharged under other than dishonorable conditions. Members of the Delaware National Guard or a Reserve unit located within Delaware with at least 20 years of membership also qualify, as do unmarried widows/widowers of eligible veterans and spouses of active-duty members who are missing in action or detained 90+ days, or spouses of disabled veterans. Preference applies only to original entrance to State Merit employment, not to promotion or retention in a reduction in force. Applicants submit DD-214 (veterans, reservists with active duty, unmarried surviving spouses), Form 1300 (spouses of missing/captured/detained members), Form NGB-22 (National Guard members/spouses), or Form DD256 (reservists without active duty) by 4:30 p.m. the business day following the job posting's closing date.
findings.value: 10 preference points (disabled veterans) or 5 preference points (other eligible veterans) added to State Merit hiring ranking score
otherReqs: Honorable discharge or discharge under other than dishonorable conditions
Applies only to original entrance to State Merit employment, not promotion or RIF retention
Documentation (DD-214, Form 1300, NGB-22, or DD256 depending on category) due by 4:30pm the business day after the job posting closes
findings.agency: Delaware Office of Management and Budget / State Jobs
findings.form: DD-214, Form 1300, Form NGB-22, or Form DD256 (category-dependent)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans who successfully meet the minimum qualifications and any special qualifications for the position will be granted appropriate preference points which will be added to their total ranking score. Ten points for disabled veterans and five points for other eligible veterans. Preference shall be confined to original entrance to State Merit employment and shall not be applied to promotion within the classified service or to retention in case of reduction in force.

findings.name: Educational Benefits for Children of Deceased Veterans and Others
findings.description: Delaware's Higher Education Office (DHEO) administers a scholarship covering tuition and required fees for the child (age 16-24) of a member of the armed forces whose death was service-related, who is being held or was held as a prisoner of war, or who is officially declared missing in action. The applicant must be a Delaware resident for three or more consecutive years prior to applying, and if the parent was a service member, the parent must have been a Delaware resident at the time of death or POW/MIA declaration. Award priority sequences across Delaware public, Delaware private, and out-of-state institutions depending on program availability. Applicants must file the FAFSA and complete the scholarship application through DHEO's Student Account Access portal by the annual May deadline.
findings.value: Tuition and required fees covered, sequenced by Delaware public / Delaware private / out-of-state institution priority
otherReqs: Applicant must be age 16-24
Delaware resident for 3+ consecutive years before application
Parent (service member) must have been a Delaware resident at time of death, POW status, or MIA declaration
FAFSA filing required
Annual application deadline (typically mid-May)
findings.agency: Delaware Higher Education Office (DHEO), Dept. of Education
documentation: Proof of parent's service-related death, POW status, or MIA declaration
findings.sourceExcerpt: Applicants must be age 16 to 24 and a resident of Delaware for three or more consecutive years before the application date. The applicant must be the child of a member of the armed forces whose death was service-related, who is being held or was held as a prisoner of war, or who is officially declared missing in action. Award covers tuition and required fees.

findings.name: Delaware Veterans Home (Milford)
findings.description: The Delaware Veterans Home, established 2007 on 24 acres in Milford, provides skilled nursing care across four units (144 total beds), offering both Long Term Care and Short Term & Rehab Care. Eligibility requires honorable discharge from active service (peacetime or wartime) with a minimum of 180 days of service (or qualifying alternative service such as National Guard overseas service, reservist status with 180+ days, or Gold Star family membership), residency in Delaware for at least one year before applying, and a medically determined need for a long-term level of care. Applicants download and submit the application and VA Form 10-10EZ along with supporting documentation to the Admissions Coordinator.
findings.value: Skilled nursing / long-term and short-term rehabilitative care
otherReqs: Honorable discharge with minimum 180 days of service (or qualifying National Guard/Reservist/Gold Star family alternative)
Delaware residency for at least 1 year before applying
Medically determined need for long-term level of care
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge

Reside in the State of Delaware for at least one year before applying for admission. Medically determined need for a long-term level of care.
